Well, hi Dr. [Name]. Um, thank you for seeing me. So, I guess... well, my wife actually kind of pushed me to make the appointment, to be honest. I mean, what made me finally bring it up and come in today is that, for the past few weeks, my eating has just been completely off. 

And it's strange because, you know, being out of work right now, my schedule is already a bit all over the place, but I usually still make a point to eat. But lately, I’ll just wake up and the whole morning goes by, and I’ll skip breakfast without even meaning to. And then lunch rolls around, and again, I don't even realize I'm skipping it. It's not like I'm trying to diet or lose weight or anything like that. I just... I don't know, the time passes and I haven't eaten a single thing. 

And then by the time dinner comes, my wife—she's a really great cook, she puts a lot of effort into our meals—she'll make something nice, and I just sit there and pick at my plate. I can tell it bothers her because she worked hard on it, but I just can't bring myself to actually eat a full meal. And I really started to notice the physical effect of it the other day when I was getting dressed, because my jeans are starting to feel really loose. Like, my regular everyday jeans that usually fit perfectly, they were just sagging, and I actually had to pull my belt a whole notch tighter just to keep them up. So, yeah, that's really what's been happening and why she wanted me to come talk to somebody...
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I guess... I mean, "down" is probably a good word for it, but it’s almost more than that, you know? It's like this physical weight. Most days lately, I wake up and there is just this really heavy, flat feeling right from the moment I open my eyes. And since I'm not working right now, my wife heads out to her job and I'm just left there by myself, and the apartment just feels... I don't know, too quiet? Like, oppressively quiet. 

Normally, when it gets like that, or if I just have some down time, I’d pick up my guitar. I’ve played since I was a teenager—mostly just acoustic, you know, messing around with some chords and fingerpicking, nothing professional, but it’s always been my go-to way to clear my head or cheer myself up. But lately... I’ll look at it sitting on the stand in the corner, and even if I do actually force myself to pick it up and play a little bit, it doesn’t really lift me at all. It just feels like I’m holding a piece of wood. There's no joy in it, no spark whatsoever. So I usually just put it right back down and go sit on the couch. It's just this constant flatness, and nothing I try really seems to break through it...
How long have you been feeling this way, and would you say your mood has been consistently low every day, or does it come and go?

Well, if I really sit down and think about it—and my wife and I were actually just talking about this the other night when she brought up making this appointment—it hasn't just been a sudden thing. It's been hanging around for a while. I'd say, looking back, this whole depressed, just completely slowed-down pattern has been hovering over me for about three months now. 

But to answer your question about whether it's every single day... it's more like it's been off and on for most of that time. Like, back in the beginning of it, a couple months ago, I'd have a few days where I felt like I was moving through molasses, just totally drained and flat, but then maybe I'd have a day where the fog would lift just enough that I could get up and run an errand, or, you know, at least pretend everything was fine for a few hours. I might even manage to do the dishes or something around the apartment. So it wasn't this unbroken chain of awful days right from the start. It would kind of weave in and out, which I guess is why I didn't make a big deal out of it at first. I just figured I was in a funk because of the job situation.

But then, recently... I'd say the past few weeks specifically, it's become so much more noticeable. That's when the off-and-on kind of stopped giving me a break and just became this constant heavy blanket. Like I was saying with the meals and the guitar, it's just every single day now. The past few weeks have just been relentless. So, yeah, I guess about three months total of this weird, sluggish, off-and-on feeling, but these last few weeks are really where it hit a wall and stayed there. It's just exhausting, honestly, waking up and wondering if today is gonna be another one of those heavy days, and lately, it just always is.
Have you lost pleasure or interest in other activities besides playing guitar, things you used to enjoy doing?

Um, I don't... I don't really think so? I mean, it’s kind of hard to say, honestly, because I’ve never really been one of those guys with a million different hobbies or, you know, a packed schedule, especially lately. The guitar was always my main thing. Like, if I had a free hour or just needed to unwind, that’s what I was doing. So it’s definitely the most obvious one to me. 

Other than that... I mean, since I’ve been out of work, my world has gotten pretty small anyway. I guess you could say I used to enjoy just, I don't know, going for a walk with my wife on the weekends or watching a movie together, and now I just kind of sit there on the couch while the TV is on. I don't really do much of *anything* right now. I just sort of exist in the apartment. 

I’ll flip through the channels during the day, maybe put on some sports or the news, but I’m not really engaged in it. But, you know, I was never a die-hard sports fanatic to begin with, so I can't really say I lost interest in it, it's just... it's just background noise to fill up that oppressive quiet I was talking about earlier. I'll just stare at the screen for hours and not even know what I watched. So, yeah, if you're asking about like, specific hobbies or passions besides the guitar, no, not really. There isn't really anything else I can point to and say, "Oh, I used to love doing that and now I don't." It's really just the guitar that stands out as the big thing I've dropped.

No, not really. I mean, obviously, being out of work isn't great for the ego, you know? It's not like I'm walking around feeling like a million bucks when my wife is the one going out and bringing home a paycheck every day while I'm just sitting on the couch watching daytime TV. But it's not like this overwhelming sense of worthlessness or anything dramatic like that. 

I guess... I mean, sure, I get frustrated with myself sometimes. But I wouldn't say I'm beating myself up over it constantly or feeling like I'm some terrible person. I know the job market is tough right now, and I know I'll find something eventually. It's just... it's just this heavy, slow feeling that's keeping me from doing much, not really my thoughts telling me I'm worthless, if that makes sense. I just feel kind of stuck, but I don't think I'm blaming myself for every little thing that goes wrong.

And it's never about anything good, either. It's always the stressful stuff. I end up feeling completely exhausted and tired before the day even officially starts. It’s just this cycle where I wake up tired, drag myself through the day feeling heavy, and then can't even get a good night's sleep to fix it. So yeah, the sleep is definitely not great right now.
